rca: The external8764 wrapper proves source bytes/modes/blobIDs and exact157 metadata but never observes the spawned SHADOW worker sys.modules.
The native stress launcher uses multiprocessing spawn, so its worker has independent module state. External or launcher-only snapshots cannot attest the real worker.
A retained-module snapshot cannot detect an alien module executed and then removed from sys.modules. Actual import/exec audit events supply a separate bounded observation window.

source_and_environment.binding: All five CLI fields together or none. Raw local Git commit/all tree hashes plus complete physical namespace SHA/modes/blobIDs must agree with the index. Helper must itself be the pinned source member.
source_and_environment.parent_preflight: Exact installed157 names/versions and policy hash locks, actual supported Python3.11.16 or3.12.14 Linux/x86_64/glibc>=2.36 virtualenv and effective sys.path before fixture_database. Installed metadata is not installed-wheel byte authentication.
source_and_environment.worker_preflight: Actual spawned worker repeats exact157 qualification before product imports, with its own executable/prefix and explicit statement that PRIMARY fixtures were already created by its parent.
source_and_environment.physical_code_proof_after: The external governed wrapper must still verify wholeSource/index/tar after actual reap. This helper does not replace that independent final source proof.

observation.parent: Snapshot and audit window cover fixture construction, launcher activity and actual PAPER exits, ending before final result emission.
observation.worker: Installed before product imports; snapshot before/after PRE+OPEN+readCommitted. Initial IMPORT_PROVENANCE event survives a later timeout; final proof rides existing FINAL.
observation.retained_scope: Actual module file/spec/namespace locations at two boundaries. No claim that retained modules enumerate every transient import.
observation.transient_scope: Stdlib audit hook counts actual import and exec events, retaining bounded module/filename strings and complete event counters. It never profiles Python function calls.
observation.callback_cost: Python calls every registered audit hook for other audit events too; this handler immediately returns for them. The spawned-worker qualification, observations and IPC consume the existing parent-managed90s window without renewal. Parent preflight/initial snapshot and fixture construction precede that original timer; parent final capture follows worker cleanup. The external wrapper must measure full launcher lifetime/resource use as well; none of these stages is relabeled as a90s whole-launcher deadline.
observation.records: At most2048 event records,2048 pending names,2048 retained-origin/unresolved records per snapshot and4096 characters per identifier (UTF-8 may occupy up to16384 bytes). Counters explicitly record overflow and errors; no truncation is silently accepted.
observation.filename_none: Original None counts retained. A named event may be resolved only through the actual final retained-module origin; missing/unresolved names remain UNVERIFIED.
observation.opaque: Generic <string>, frozen-looking exec filenames and other unknown code locations remain opaque/UNVERIFIED. No generic allowlist is used to turn them GREEN.
observation.closure_limit: Bootstrap before installation and postboundary IPC/emission/process teardown are outside the observed window. Local module paths/code.co_filename are interpreter metadata, not cryptographic authentication of executed code or installed binaries.
observation.cleanup: Owner wrappers unconditionally deactivate audit hooks on every exit, including root/fixture/spawn/import/setup failures. Python audit hooks cannot be uninstalled; inactive hooks return without changing counters.

pid_and_acceptance.worker_binding: Both initial/final worker payloads must match ctx.Process.pid, os.getppid==launcherPID and sourceSHA/tree/indexRAWsha. Actual child.join/exitcode/cleanup and final receipt are required. No manual wait4 is added to multiprocessing's own waitpid.
pid_and_acceptance.external_wrapper: Future wrapper must bind native launcher os.getpid to external Popen.pid and actual wait4/reap/returncode. Its own sys.modules cannot substitute for the spawned worker proof.
pid_and_acceptance.incomplete: Business/resource-complete can coexist with import proof incomplete. In opt-in audit mode incomplete imports raise StressImportProofLimit with lossless evidence/exit1. Missing FINAL, timeout, invalid PID/pin, unknown origin, opaque exec, observer failure or overflow never closes the proof.
pid_and_acceptance.legacy: No binding preserves original business path and reports NOT_AUDITED. Old8764 and other raw epochs remain byteexact and are never relabeled as audited.
